title: Resolver cache redispatch causes occasional cross-tenant DNS resolution after peering flap
creator: Owen Park
description: Summary: Multiple Dedicated customers reported intermittent cross-tenant DNS resolution observed immediately after VPC peering switchover events. Symptoms included tenants resolving private hostnames that belonged to a different tenant for short windows (30s-3m) following peering failovers or rekey/peering control-plane updates. Root cause appears tied to a shared resolver cache and 'redispatch' logic that re-uses cached entries when resolver workers are rebalanced during peering transitions.
impact_details: Affects Dedicated clusters using the shared forwarder/resolver process on nodes with peering-enabled egress. Customers saw transient misrouting of traffic to other tenants' internal hostnames (no host-level data exfiltration observed), causing application errors and increased support load. Multiple production escalations opened: ACME-2319, MedApp-1197. Approx 7 tenants impacted over 3 incidents since 2026-02-26.
reproduction_steps: Provision two tenants A and B on the same Dedicated cluster with VPC peering enabled.
Create short-lived internal hostnames (a.internal.svc and b.internal.svc) and a forwarding resolver with shared worker pool.
Trigger a peering control-plane change that causes worker rebalancing (simulate by rotating peering keys or toggling route announce briefly).
Immediately after the flap, issue repeated DNS queries from tenant A for b.internal.svc and observe cached answers being served for 30s-3m windows.
Collect resolver logs showing cache hits and old namespace bindings and confirm tenant id mismatch in resolved metadata.
Observed on kernel: ubuntu-6.1 nodes, resolver version fwd-2.7.1.
observed_metrics_and_logs: Spike in resolver_cache_hit_rate for keys scoped without tenant-id: +200% during peering event windows
Customer errors: connection refused / unexpected host header in app logs during window
Dashboard: dedicated/peering/events and dedicated/dns/error-rate correlated at T+10s to T+180s
root_cause: The shared forwarder/resolver used a cache key that omitted tenant-scoped metadata in a small percentage of code paths. During peering worker rebalances (triggered by rekey or route updates), cached entries were re-dispatched to newly assigned workers without re-attaching the correct tenant namespace. This allowed stale cache entries to be served to the wrong tenant for the duration of the cached TTL or until invalidation.
mitigation_taken: 2026-02-27 03:12 UTC: Emergency mitigation - disabled resolver redispatch on affected pools (config flag: forwarder.redispatch=false)
2026-02-27 03:45 UTC: Issued forced cache invalidation for all peering-enabled nodes (invalidate keyspace matching internal.svc patterns)
Notified affected customers with temporary workaround to add short-lived client-side DNS TTLs and health-check backoffs
Scoped rollout: prevented autoscaler from moving resolver pods between nodes during ongoing investigation
proposed_fix: 1) Tighten cache key to always include tenant_id and peering-session-id. 2) Add peering-change hooks to proactively invalidate per-tenant cache entries on peering control-plane events. 3) Add an invariant check in the forwarder: when serving a cached entry, assert tenant_id matches request context and reject+fallback if mismatch. 4) Add unit and integration tests that simulate worker rebalance and ensure no cross-tenant cache leaks.
implementation_notes: Code changes in repo: infra/forwarder: change cacheKey(context, qname) to include context.tenant_id and context.peering_session
Add peering event listener in control-plane agent to emit cache-invalidate events to forwarder via existing pub/sub channel
Backwards compatibility: config param forwarder.cache_strict_tenant=true default enabled for Dedicated runtime-1.22
Performance: microbenchmark shows 3% overhead on cache key computation; acceptable vs correctness tradeoff
rollout_plan: Create PR and land unit tests (canary branch): PR #8142
Canary: deploy to 2 non-prod Dedicated clusters and run integration scenario for 48 hours
Stage: deploy to 20% of runtime-1.22 Dedicated clusters during low-traffic window (overnight UTC)
Full rollout: 3-day staggered rollout with automated health checks; immediate rollback trigger if dns_error_rate > baseline + 5%
Customer remediation: notify affected tenants and provide option for targeted invalidation if they prefer immediate remediation
testing_plan: Unit tests for cache key composition and tenant-assertion failure paths
Integration test harness simulating peering rekey and worker rebalance; verify no tenant mismatch across 10k queries
Chaos test: random pod restarts during peering events in staging cluster
Load test: verify p50/p95/p99 DNS latency change < 10% after change
safety_and_security_notes: No data exfiltration observed; issue limited to name resolution mapping. Still requires security review for any cache key changes touching tenant identifiers. KMS/HSM not involved.
